# audi_arg3_pause — deployed as `audi-arg3-pause`

A NOVA app (FastAPI via NOVAx, on the [NOVA Python SDK](https://github.com/wandelbotsgmbh/wandelbots-nova))
that reproduces a **robot that stays in standstill at the start of an execution although its
enable signal allows motion** — one cycle finishes normally, the next is commanded with the same
condition and the robot never starts.

Per robot the operator picks a TCP, a base-joint (joint 0) rotation from the presets
5/10/15/20/45/90 degrees (default 10) and a direction. Each cycle rotates joint 0 by that amount
and back, executed with **`pause_on_io` armed on the enable signal**: the robot is allowed to
move while that signal reads `true`, and the controller pauses it on path as soon as it reads
`false`. The SDK waits for the signal to come back and resumes, so one `execute()` covers any
number of pauses (see the SDK's `docs/architecture/adr/002-io-pause-is-resumable.md`).

## How this differs from the other apps in this repo

**Nothing waits for the signal before the motion.** The move-up apps gate the loop with
`wait_for_bus_io` on `start` and only then execute. Here the gating *is* the thing under test,
so the execution is always commanded and the controller decides whether the robot moves.

That means the shared UI's **"wait IO" field is this app's enable signal** (default `start`),
not a pre-motion gate. `stop` ends the loop as in every other app. Both are created on a virtual
bus-IO service with the ＋ button next to the fields.

Because an execution can legitimately sit still for as long as the signal is low, `execute()` is
**not** bounded by a wall-clock timeout here (`MOTION_TIMEOUT_S` defaults to `0`). A wedged robot
therefore stays wedged, on purpose — that is the state worth capturing. **`Stop all` in the UI is
the way out**: the stop IO is only polled between cycles, so a robot inside `execute()` never
sees it.

`fail_after_stall_s` is the bound that fits this app better, because it only counts time during
which the robot *was* allowed to move. Leave it at 0 while watching a single robot; set it for
an unattended `auto_resume` run.

## Run it

```bash
uv sync --locked
NOVA_API=http://<instance> uv run python -m audi_arg3_pause
open http://localhost:3000/ui
```

`GET /api/health` tells you which instance and cell the app is actually talking to. Confirm the
controllers are virtual before starting anything that moves.

One robot without the app, from a shell:

```bash
uv run python -m audi_arg3_pause.run_program ir340r01 --tcp 1 --wait-io start --stall-s 10
```

## The three scenarios

`scenario` decides how the enable signal is driven during a run. **Only `manual`
never writes it** — on a real cell it is a PLC-facing Profinet variable that the sibling apps
also use as their run-enable, so an app that writes it is gating every other ARG3 robot too.

| scenario | what it does | what it answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`manual`** (default) | never touches the signal; you toggle it | anything, by hand |
| **`enabled_once`** | waits until the signal *already* allows motion, commands exactly **one** execution, finishes | does a clean execution with nothing to pause it start at all? No pause and no resume are involved, so a robot that does not move here failed from a standing start |
| **`auto_resume`** | per cycle: drop the signal, command the execution (robot held at the trajectory start), wait `enable_delay_ms`, raise it again | the pause/resume path, unattended — one resume attempt every ~4 s, so a rate instead of anecdotes |

`enabled_once` runs **one execution per process** on purpose: the question is whether the
*first* execution moves, and looping inside one process would reuse a warm SDK instead of
testing a cold one. Click *Run selected* again for another trial, and count.

`auto_resume` is the statistics engine. On the virtual cell it turns over a full
hold → execute → release → move → complete cycle every ~4.3 s, so an hour is ~800 resume
attempts. Set `fail_after_stall_s` for it (60 is sensible) so a wedge ends the cycle instead
of parking the robot until someone notices.

## Run options

| option | default | what it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scenario` | manual | see above; the only option that makes the app write an IO |
| `enable_delay_ms` | 1000 | `auto_resume`: how long the robot is held before the signal is raised |
| `fail_after_stall_s` | 0 (never) | cancel an execution that has been allowed to move but standing still this long |
| `degrees` / `direction` | 10, positive | the joint-0 rotation, same presets as `../tcpswitch` |
| `state_rate_ms` | 0 (step rate) | the **execution's** state stream rate — the stream the SDK's state machine reads to decide a pause happened and a resume happened |
| `stall_s` | 10 | how long "enabled, standing still, not advancing" must hold before it is reported; 0 switches the detector off |
| `gap_ms` | 0 | idle time between cycles — separates a back-to-back race from a state that is simply wrong |
| `replan` | off | plan once and execute many (off) or plan afresh each cycle (on) |
| `verbose` | off | DEBUG for the SDK's `move_forward`, trajectory cursor, state machine and `io_condition` loggers |

Environment knobs that are not per-run: `OBSERVE_STATE_RATE_MS` (100; the observer's own stream,
`-1` disables it), `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_S` (2), `STALL_REPEAT_S` (30), `MOTION_TIMEOUT_S` (0),
`STATE_RESPONSE_RATE_MS` / `STALL_S` (the defaults the UI prefills), plus the usual
`NOVA_API`, `CELL_NAME`, `LOG_DIR`, `LOG_LEVEL`.

## Resume strategy (`resume`, `missed_auto_resume`)

Branch `pause-auto-resume`. Who restarts the motion after an IO pause -- not to be confused
with the `auto_resume` *scenario*, which is about the app driving the enable signal:

| `resume` | what goes on the wire | while held | who resumes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sdk` (default) | `PauseOnIO` as before | `PAUSED_ON_IO` | the SDK sends a new start once the signal allows motion |
| `controller` | `PauseOnIO.auto_resume = true` | `RUNNING` while braking, then `WAIT_FOR_IO` | the controller, by itself (robotics/wbr!2384) |

`missed_auto_resume` only applies to `controller`: when the signal allows motion but the robot
is still held 500 ms later, `fail` (default) ends the execution ("AUTO-RESUME MISSED") so an
upstream defect stays visible, `start` sends one start from the SDK to keep the cell moving.

`controller` needs a RAE image with wbr!2384 *and* an API client that knows the field: both apps
pin `wandelbots-api-client 26.8.0+a3081.4275fd77.483450` (service-manager MR !3081) from the
internal GitLab registry (project 889, readable without credentials, `[[tool.uv.index]]`
`wandelbots-internal`). On an image without wbr!2384 the controller ignores the flag, the pause is
a terminal `PAUSED_ON_IO` again, and with `fail` the run fails at the first release -- which is
also the quickest way to find out what the image does. Roll back: check out `pause-on-io-repro`.

## Reading a log

Every run's log opens with what was configured, the **exact condition sent to the controller**
and the installed `wandelbots-nova` version — so a log always says which SDK produced it, which
matters while the pin moves along the interlock branch.

Two observers then run for the whole program and write into the same file:

- the **enable signal**, watched over NATS (the same push the SDK's own condition watcher
  reads), logging every change;
- the **motion group's own state stream**, on its own websocket, logging transitions of the
  trajectory state (`Running` / `PausedOnIO` / `PausedByUser` / `Ended`), `standstill` and the
  trajectory location.

While an `execute()` is open, a heartbeat prints both side by side every two seconds:

```
cycle 3 -- in execute() 12.0s (beat #6) | enable 'start'=True for 14.5s
         | stop 'stop'=False for 14.4s | traj=PausedOnIO standstill=True loc=0.0000 for 10.2s
         frames=138 | allowed to move
```

and the detector turns the claim into one greppable block:

```
cycle 3 -- STALL: allowed to move but standing still for 10.2s (report #1)
    enable enable 'start'=True for 14.5s, 1 change(s) this run
    traj=PausedOnIO standstill=True loc=0.0000 for 10.2s frames=138
    travelled 0.0000 in this execute() -- the execution never started
    last state frame 0.09s ago, execute() open 12.0s
    the pause condition is 'start == False'; the signal reads True, so it does NOT hold
    and the controller should be running this trajectory
```

`grep STALL` is the whole triage. A separate `LINGER` warning covers the neighbouring case —
the trajectory reached its end and `execute()` has not returned yet — so a slow websocket
teardown is never mistaken for a robot that will not start. The two are told apart by how far
the location travelled *in that execution*, not by the trajectory state alone: a terminal frame
with zero travel is a fault, not a completion.

## Minimal repro without the app

`scripts/pause_repro.py` is the same program as a single, UI-less SDK script for handing to
colleagues or to the SDK team: plain `@nova.program` + `run_program`, configured by environment
variables, with both observers and the same stall reporting inlined.

```bash
# manual: you toggle the signal
NOVA_API=http://<ipc> CONTROLLER=ir340r01 TCP=1 ENABLE_IO=start STOP_IO=stop \
  DEGREES=10 CYCLES=0 STALL_S=10 VERBOSE=true \
  uv run python scripts/pause_repro.py

# one execution with the signal already high
SCENARIO=enabled_once uv run python scripts/pause_repro.py

# unattended pause/resume, one attempt every few seconds
SCENARIO=auto_resume ENABLE_DELAY_MS=1000 uv run python scripts/pause_repro.py
```

It only needs `wandelbots-nova` installed (any environment with the SDK works), so the file can
be copied out of this repo on its own.

## Checking the detector without a cell

The fault has not reproduced on a virtual cell, so the one piece that has to be right when it
finally happens is the piece a virtual cell cannot exercise: the rule that decides STALL vs
LINGER vs silence. It has offline checks — no instance, no network:

```bash
uv run python scripts/check_stall_detector.py     # 11 cases
```

## Deploy

Exactly like `../sdk`: `skaffold dev --cleanup=false --status-check=false` for development
(hot-reloads `.py` changes into the pod), `nova app install` for the slow path. `k8s/app.yaml`
is the NOVA `App` resource; it sets neither `NOVA_API` nor `BASE_PATH` on purpose (the
app-operator injects both) and mounts a 300Mi volume at `/data` for the log files.

"""Factory that creates the pause-on-IO repro program for one robot controller.

The program reproduces a robot that **stays in standstill at the start of an
execution although its enable signal says it may move**, seen on the physical
cell with the SDK's ``pause_on_io`` mechanism: one cycle finishes normally, the
next one is commanded with the same condition and the robot never starts.

Each generated program loops:

1. Check the stop IO -- exit the loop when the stop condition is met.
2. ``execute()`` the trajectory with ``pause_on_io`` armed on the enable
   signal. The robot is allowed to move while that signal reads ``True``; the
   controller pauses it on path as soon as it reads ``False`` and the SDK
   resumes once it is back (see the SDK's
   ``docs/architecture/adr/002-io-pause-is-resumable.md``).
3. Go back to step 1.

**There is deliberately no wait for the signal before the motion.** The move-up
apps gate the loop with ``wait_for_bus_io`` and only then execute; here the
gating *is* the thing under test, so the execution is always commanded and the
controller decides whether the robot moves. The same field of the operator UI
therefore names a different thing in this app: ``wait_io`` is the **enable
signal** handed to ``pause_on_io``, not a pre-motion gate.

What makes a failure visible is ``observe.py``: an independent watcher on the
signal and a second one on the motion group's own state stream, printed side by
side in a heartbeat while ``execute()`` is open, plus a stall detector that
reports "allowed to move but standing still" as one greppable block.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import contextlib
import logging
import math
import time
from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version

import nova

"""Factory that creates the pause-on-IO repro program for one robot controller.

The program reproduces a robot that **stays in standstill at the start of an
execution although its enable signal says it may move**, seen on the physical
cell with the SDK's ``pause_on_io`` mechanism: one cycle finishes normally, the
next one is commanded with the same condition and the robot never starts.

Each generated program loops:

1. Check the stop IO -- exit the loop when the stop condition is met.
2. ``execute()`` the trajectory with ``pause_on_io`` armed on the enable
   signal. The robot is allowed to move while that signal reads ``True``; the
   controller pauses it on path as soon as it reads ``False`` and the SDK
   resumes once it is back (see the SDK's
   ``docs/architecture/adr/002-io-pause-is-resumable.md``).
3. Go back to step 1.

**There is deliberately no wait for the signal before the motion.** The move-up
apps gate the loop with ``wait_for_bus_io`` and only then execute; here the
gating *is* the thing under test, so the execution is always commanded and the
controller decides whether the robot moves. The same field of the operator UI
therefore names a different thing in this app: ``wait_io`` is the **enable
signal** handed to ``pause_on_io``, not a pre-motion gate.

What makes a failure visible is ``observe.py``: an independent watcher on the
signal and a second one on the motion group's own state stream, printed side by
side in a heartbeat while ``execute()`` is open, plus a stall detector that
reports "allowed to move but standing still" as one greppable block.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import contextlib
import logging
import math
import time
from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version
from typing import Literal

import nova
from decouple import config
from nova import api
from nova.actions import joint_ptp
from nova.cell import motion_enable_signal
from nova.events import Cycle, novax_cycle
from nova.program.function import Program
from nova.types import MotionSettings
from nova.utils.io import IOChange, get_bus_io_value, set_bus_io_value, wait_for_bus_io
from novax.config import CELL_NAME
from wandelbots_api_client.v2_pydantic.models.models import SettableRobotSystemMode

from audi_arg3_pause import logs
from audi_arg3_pause.observe import ExecutionObserver

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MOTION_TIMEOUT_S = config("MOTION_TIMEOUT_S", default=0.0, cast=float)
"""Hard bound on one execute(), or 0 to disable it -- and disabled is the default here.

The siblings bound ``execute()`` at 300 s because a wedged execution there is
always a fault. In this app an execution that sits still can be completely
correct: with the enable signal low the robot is *supposed* to wait, for as long
as the operator leaves it low. A timeout would also destroy the wedged state
that the run exists to capture, so the stall detector reports instead and the
run keeps going.

``fail_after_stall_s`` is the bound that fits this app better, because it only
fires while the robot *is* allowed to move. Both are applied by
``ExecutionObserver.run_execution``, which owns the motion task.
"""

# Trajectory locations move by more than this when the robot actually ran.
_TRAVEL_EPSILON = 1e-6

# SDK loggers that explain what the pause machinery decided. ``move_forward``
# reports every pause and resume at INFO already, so the interesting lines are
# in the log without ``verbose``; the rest are the frame-by-frame detail.
_SDK_PAUSE_LOGGERS = (
    "nova.cell.movement_controller.move_forward",
    "nova.cell.movement_controller.trajectory_cursor",
    "nova.cell.movement_controller.trajectory_state_machine",
    "nova.cell.io_condition",
)


# Run-gate IO defaults. The names match the move-up apps so the same signals
# drive every variant on a cell -- but `wait_io` means something different here
# (the enable signal for pause_on_io, see the module docstring).
DEFAULT_WAIT_IO = "start"
DEFAULT_WAIT_IO_VALUE = True
DEFAULT_STOP_IO = "stop"
DEFAULT_STOP_IO_VALUE = True

# The base-joint rotation the operator can pick, in degrees. Presets only, same
# set as ../tcpswitch.
DEGREE_PRESETS = (5, 10, 15, 20, 45, 90)
DEFAULT_DEGREES = 10
Direction = Literal["positive", "negative"]
DEFAULT_DIRECTION: Direction = "positive"

# Motion-group state stream rate in ms for the *execution*, per run. 0 = the
# controller's own step rate, requested by passing state_stream_rate_msecs=None
# -- the same meaning as in every sibling app. This is the stream the SDK's
# execution state machine reads, so it is a plausible variable in a pause bug;
# the observer's own stream has its own rate (OBSERVE_STATE_RATE_MS).
DEFAULT_STATE_RATE_MS = config("STATE_RESPONSE_RATE_MS", default=0, cast=int)

# How long "enabled, standing still, location not advancing" must hold inside
# one execute() before it is reported. 0 switches the detector off.
DEFAULT_STALL_S = config("STALL_S", default=10.0, cast=float)

# Pause between two cycles, in milliseconds. The reported symptom is about the
# execution that *follows* a finished one, so how much time sits between them
# is worth being able to vary.
DEFAULT_GAP_MS = 0

# Plan once and execute many (the move-up apps' shape) or plan every cycle.
DEFAULT_REPLAN = False

DEFAULT_VERBOSE = False

# How the enable signal is driven during a run.
#
# The default is the one that touches nothing: on a real cell this signal is a
# PLC-facing Profinet variable, and it is also what the sibling apps use as
# their run-enable -- so an app that writes it is driving every other ARG3 robot
# on the cell too. Automation is opt-in for that reason, and says so in the log.
SCENARIO_MANUAL = "manual"
SCENARIO_ENABLED_ONCE = "enabled_once"
SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME = "auto_resume"
SCENARIOS = (SCENARIO_MANUAL, SCENARIO_ENABLED_ONCE, SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME)
DEFAULT_SCENARIO = SCENARIO_MANUAL

SCENARIO_HELP = {
    SCENARIO_MANUAL: (
        "the app never writes the enable signal; the operator toggles it. Use this to watch "
        "a long run, or to reproduce by hand."
    ),
    SCENARIO_ENABLED_ONCE: (
        "reads the enable signal but never writes it. Waits until it already allows motion, "
        "then commands exactly ONE "
        "execution and finish. No pause and no resume are involved, so a robot that does not "
        "move here has failed to start from a clean state -- run it repeatedly, each run in a "
        "fresh process, and count."
    ),
    SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME: (
        "per cycle: drop the enable signal, command the execution (the robot is held at the "
        "start), wait `enable_delay_ms`, raise the signal again and let the cycle run. This "
        "exercises the pause/resume path unattended, which is where the wedge was observed."
    ),
}

# Who resumes an IO pause (the SDK's ExecutionPolicy.pause_resume, ADR 002 addendum).
# Not to be confused with the auto_resume *scenario* above, which is about the app
# driving the enable signal; this is about who restarts the motion afterwards.
RESUME_SDK = "sdk"
RESUME_CONTROLLER = "controller"
RESUME_STRATEGIES = (RESUME_SDK, RESUME_CONTROLLER)
DEFAULT_RESUME = RESUME_SDK
RESUME_HELP = {
    RESUME_SDK: (
        "the SDK sends a new start once the enable signal allows motion again (the controller "
        "never resumes a plain pause_on_io pause by itself)"
    ),
    RESUME_CONTROLLER: (
        "every start carries PauseOnIO.auto_resume and the controller resumes by itself "
        "(robotics/wbr!2384; needs a RAE image and API client built with it)"
    ),
}
# Under 'controller': what the SDK does when the signal allows motion but the
# controller still holds the robot after the SDK's resume_detect_s.
MISSED_FAIL = "fail"
MISSED_START = "start"
MISSED_AUTO_RESUME_CHOICES = (MISSED_FAIL, MISSED_START)
DEFAULT_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME = MISSED_FAIL

# Pause between dropping the enable signal and commanding the execution, so the
# controller has seen the new value before it is armed with the condition.
ENABLE_SETTLE_MS = config("ENABLE_SETTLE_MS", default=300, cast=int)

# Delay between an execution being commanded and the enable signal being raised
# again, in the auto_resume scenario.
DEFAULT_ENABLE_DELAY_MS = 1000

# End a cycle that has been "allowed to move but standing still" for this long.
# 0 = never, which keeps a wedge parked for inspection; set it for unattended runs.
DEFAULT_FAIL_AFTER_STALL_S = config("FAIL_AFTER_STALL_S", default=0.0, cast=float)

# Motion limits. Same reasoning as ../tcpswitch: TCP limits bound a joint PTP
# too, so a KR240's flange at ~1.5 m radius rotates at most ~8 deg/s at 200 mm/s.
TCP_VELOCITY_MM_S = config("TCP_VELOCITY_MM_S", default=200.0, cast=float)
TCP_ACCELERATION_MM_S2 = config("TCP_ACCELERATION_MM_S2", default=500.0, cast=float)
TCP_JERK_MM_S3 = config("TCP_JERK_MM_S3", default=2500.0, cast=float)

# Tag on the cycle events this app publishes (nova.v2.cells.<cell>.cycle), so a
# consumer can tell them from the other apps' cycles on the same cell.
APP_NAME = "audi-arg3-pause"
PROGRAM_SUFFIX = "_pause_on_io"


def program_id(controller_name: str) -> str:
    """The NOVAx program id for a controller -- the one place it is derived."""
    return f"{controller_name}{PROGRAM_SUFFIX}"


def validate_run_settings(
    degrees: int,
    direction: str,
    stall_s: float,
    gap_ms: int,
    scenario: str = DEFAULT_SCENARIO,
    enable_delay_ms: int = DEFAULT_ENABLE_DELAY_MS,
    resume: str = DEFAULT_RESUME,
    missed_auto_resume: str = DEFAULT_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME,
) -> None:
    """Reject bad run settings up front, with a message the operator can act on."""
    if scenario not in SCENARIOS:
        raise ValueError(f"scenario must be one of {SCENARIOS}, got '{scenario}'")
    if resume not in RESUME_STRATEGIES:
        raise ValueError(f"resume must be one of {RESUME_STRATEGIES}, got '{resume}'")
    if missed_auto_resume not in MISSED_AUTO_RESUME_CHOICES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"missed_auto_resume must be one of {MISSED_AUTO_RESUME_CHOICES}, "
            f"got '{missed_auto_resume}'"
        )
    if enable_delay_ms < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"enable_delay_ms must not be negative, got {enable_delay_ms}")
    if degrees not in DEGREE_PRESETS:
        raise ValueError(f"degrees must be one of {DEGREE_PRESETS}, got {degrees}")
    if direction not in ("positive", "negative"):
        raise ValueError(f"direction must be 'positive' or 'negative', got '{direction}'")
    if stall_s < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"stall_s must not be negative, got {stall_s}")
    if gap_ms < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"gap_ms must not be negative, got {gap_ms}")


def wire_rate(state_rate_ms: int) -> int | None:
    """``state_rate_ms`` as the SDK wants it: 0 means "don't ask for a rate"."""
    return state_rate_ms or None


def enable_condition(io: str, enable_value: bool) -> api.models.PauseOnIO:
    """The ``pause_on_io`` condition for an enable signal on bus IO ``io``.

    ``motion_enable_signal`` is the SDK's fail-safe wiring: it pauses while
    ``io == False``, so a dropped signal, a broken wire or a lost fieldbus all
    stop the robot. ``enable_value=False`` inverts that, which is what the
    operator gets by unticking the value in the UI -- it is supported so the
    field means what it says, but it is *not* fail-safe and says so in the log.
    """
    if enable_value:
        return motion_enable_signal(io, api.models.IOOrigin.BUS_IO)
    logger.warning(
        "enable IO '%s' is configured to allow motion while it reads False; this inverted "
        "wiring is NOT fail-safe (a lost bus reads False and would allow motion)",
        io,
    )
    return api.models.PauseOnIO(
        io=api.models.IOBooleanValue(io=io, value=True),
        comparator=api.models.Comparator.COMPARATOR_EQUALS,
        io_origin=api.models.IOOrigin.BUS_IO,
    )


def _set_sdk_verbosity(verbose: bool) -> None:
    """Turn the SDK's pause/cursor/state-machine loggers up for this run."""
    for name in _SDK_PAUSE_LOGGERS:
        logging.getLogger(name).setLevel(logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.NOTSET)


def _sdk_version() -> str:
    """The installed wandelbots-nova version, for the top of every run's log.

    Which SDK branch produced a log is the first question asked of it, and the
    answer must not depend on remembering what was pinned that day.
    """
    try:
        return version("wandelbots-nova")
    except PackageNotFoundError:  # pragma: no cover - only if the SDK is not installed
        return "unknown"


def _new_cycle_event(ctx: nova.ProgramContext, controller_name: str, cycle: int) -> Cycle:
    """A cycle event for one motion, published on ``nova.v2.cells.<cell>.cycle``."""
    return novax_cycle(
        ctx.cell,
        app=APP_NAME,
        program=program_id(controller_name),
        extra={"controller": controller_name, "cycle": cycle},
    )


async def _publish_cycle(publish, controller_name: str, what: str) -> None:
    """Await one of ``Cycle.start()/finish()/fail()`` without letting it hurt the run.

    A broken event bus must never stop or fail a motion. Deliberately NOT
    ``async with Cycle``: its ``__aexit__`` would swallow the motion's own
    exception, turning a failed robot into one that quietly keeps cycling.
    """
    try:
        await publish
    except Exception:
        logger.debug("%s: could not publish cycle %s event", controller_name, what, exc_info=True)


async def create_pause_program(controller_name: str, nova_instance: nova.Nova) -> Program:
    """Create the pause-on-IO program for one controller.

    The returned ``Program`` can be registered on a ``Novax`` instance; its id
    is derived from the controller name (see ``program_id``).
    """
    tcps, active_tcp = await tcp_choices(controller_name, nova_instance)
    default_tcp = active_tcp or (tcps[0] if tcps else None)

    async def _pause_on_io(
        ctx: nova.ProgramContext,
        wait_io: str,
        wait_io_value: bool,
        stop_io: str,
        stop_io_value: bool,
        tcp: str | None,
        degrees: int,
        direction: str,
        state_rate_ms: int,
        stall_s: float,
        gap_ms: int,
        replan: bool,
        verbose: bool,
        scenario: str,
        enable_delay_ms: int,
        fail_after_stall_s: float,
        resume: str,
        missed_auto_resume: str,
    ) -> None:
        validate_run_settings(
            degrees,
            direction,
            stall_s,
            gap_ms,
            scenario,
            enable_delay_ms,
            resume,
            missed_auto_resume,
        )
        _set_sdk_verbosity(verbose)
        _apply_resume_strategy(controller_name, resume, missed_auto_resume)
        sign = 1.0 if direction == "positive" else -1.0
        delta_rad = sign * math.radians(degrees)

        controller = await ctx.cell.controller(controller_name)
        motion_group = controller[0]
        pause_on_io = enable_condition(wait_io, wait_io_value)

        logger.info(
            "%s: pause-on-IO repro -- enable IO '%s' allows motion while it reads %s, stop IO "
            "'%s' ends the loop at %s",
            controller_name,
            wait_io,
            wait_io_value,
            stop_io,
            stop_io_value,
        )
        logger.info(
            "%s: tcp=%s, joint 0 %s%d deg and back, state_rate=%s, stall_s=%.1f, gap_ms=%d, "
            "replan=%s, verbose=%s, motion_timeout=%s, fail_after_stall=%s",
            controller_name,
            tcp,
            "+" if sign > 0 else "-",
            degrees,
            f"{state_rate_ms} ms" if state_rate_ms else "controller step rate",
            stall_s,
            gap_ms,
            replan,
            verbose,
            f"{MOTION_TIMEOUT_S:.0f}s" if MOTION_TIMEOUT_S > 0 else "disabled",
            f"{fail_after_stall_s:.0f}s" if fail_after_stall_s > 0 else "disabled",
        )
        logger.info("%s: scenario '%s' -- %s", controller_name, scenario, SCENARIO_HELP[scenario])
        if scenario == SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME:
            # The only scenario that drives the signal. It is a PLC-facing
            # variable that the sibling apps use as their run-enable, so an app
            # writing it is driving every other ARG3 robot on the cell too.
            logger.warning(
                "%s: this run WRITES the enable IO '%s' itself, once per cycle. On a shared "
                "cell that signal also gates the sibling apps' robots.",
                controller_name,
                wait_io,
            )
        if scenario == SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME and fail_after_stall_s <= 0:
            logger.warning(
                "%s: scenario '%s' is meant to run unattended but fail_after_stall_s is 0, so a "
                "wedged cycle will park the robot until someone stops it",
                controller_name,
                scenario,
            )
        logger.info(
            "%s: wandelbots-nova %s; pause condition sent to the controller: %s",
            controller_name,
            _sdk_version(),
            pause_on_io.model_dump_json(),
        )

        # Switch controller default usage to control mode before moving.
        await ctx.nova.api.controller_api.set_default_mode(
            cell=CELL_NAME,
            controller=controller_name,
            mode=SettableRobotSystemMode.MODE_CONTROL,
        )

        settings = MotionSettings(
            tcp_velocity_limit=TCP_VELOCITY_MM_S,
            REDACTED,
            tcp_jerk_limit=TCP_JERK_MM_S3,
        )

        # Home is read once: every cycle rotates away from and back to the same
        # joint configuration, so the robot never drifts across cycles.
        home = tuple(await motion_group.joints())
        target = (home[0] + delta_rad,) + home[1:]
        actions = [joint_ptp(target, settings=settings), joint_ptp(home, settings=settings)]
        logger.info(
            "%s: home joints %s, joint 0 target %.4f rad", controller_name, _fmt(home), target[0]
        )

        async with ExecutionObserver(
            ctx.nova, CELL_NAME, controller_name, motion_group.id, wait_io, stop_io
        ) as observer:
            trajectory = None
            if not replan:
                trajectory = await _plan(motion_group, actions, tcp, controller_name, 0)

            cycle = 0
            while True:
                # 1. Check the stop IO -- exit when the stop condition is met.
                if await _should_stop(ctx.nova, stop_io, stop_io_value):
                    logger.info(
                        "%s: stop IO '%s' is %s, exiting loop",
                        controller_name,
                        stop_io,
                        stop_io_value,
                    )
                    break

                cycle += 1

                # 2. Put the enable signal where this scenario wants it before
                #    the execution is commanded (see SCENARIOS).
                if scenario == SCENARIO_ENABLED_ONCE:
                    await _wait_for_enable(ctx.nova, wait_io, wait_io_value, controller_name, cycle)
                elif scenario == SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME:
                    await _write_enable(
                        ctx.nova, wait_io, not wait_io_value, controller_name, cycle, "holding"
                    )
                    # Let the controller see the new value before it is armed
                    # with the condition; otherwise the execution can start
                    # before the signal it is supposed to be held by arrives.
                    await asyncio.sleep(ENABLE_SETTLE_MS / 1000.0)

                logger.info(
                    "%s: cycle %d -- commanding execute() | %s",
                    controller_name,
                    cycle,
                    observer.snapshot(),
                )

                if replan:
                    trajectory = await _plan(motion_group, actions, tcp, controller_name, cycle)

                # 3. Execute with the pause condition armed. A failure is
                #    reported and re-raised: no retries around motions.
                cycle_event = _new_cycle_event(ctx, controller_name, cycle)
                await _publish_cycle(cycle_event.start(), controller_name, "started")
                started = time.monotonic()
                releaser = None
                if scenario == SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME:
                    releaser = asyncio.create_task(
                        _release_after(
                            ctx.nova,
                            wait_io,
                            wait_io_value,
                            enable_delay_ms,
                            controller_name,
                            cycle,
                        ),
                        name=f"auto-release-{controller_name}-{cycle}",
                    )
                try:
                    await observer.run_execution(
                        cycle,
                        motion_group.execute(
                            trajectory,
                            tcp,
                            actions,
                            pause_on_io=pause_on_io,
                            state_stream_rate_msecs=wire_rate(state_rate_ms),
                        ),
                        stall_s=stall_s,
                        fail_after_stall_s=fail_after_stall_s,
                        hard_timeout_s=MOTION_TIMEOUT_S,
                    )
                except Exception as exc:
                    reason = str(exc) or type(exc).__name__
                    logger.error(
                        "%s: cycle %d FAILED after %.3fs, travelled %.4f: %s | %s",
                        controller_name,
                        cycle,
                        time.monotonic() - started,
                        observer.trajectory.window_span,
                        reason,
                        observer.snapshot(),
                    )
                    await _publish_cycle(cycle_event.fail(reason), controller_name, "failed")
                    raise
                finally:
                    if releaser is not None:
                        releaser.cancel()
                        with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                            await releaser
                await _publish_cycle(cycle_event.finish(), controller_name, "finished")
                logger.info(
                    "%s: cycle %d complete -- execute() returned after %.3fs, travelled %.4f | %s",
                    controller_name,
                    cycle,
                    time.monotonic() - started,
                    observer.trajectory.window_span,
                    observer.snapshot(),
                )
                _report_verdict(controller_name, cycle, observer.trajectory.window_span)

                # 4. One execution is the whole experiment in the pre-enabled
                #    scenario: a fresh process per trial is the point, because
                #    the question is whether the *first* execution moves.
                if scenario == SCENARIO_ENABLED_ONCE:
                    logger.info(
                        "%s: scenario '%s' runs a single execution -- finishing",
                        controller_name,
                        scenario,
                    )
                    break

                if gap_ms:
                    await asyncio.sleep(gap_ms / 1000.0)

            logger.info("%s: finished after %d cycles", controller_name, cycle)

    @nova.program(
        id=program_id(controller_name),
        name=f"{controller_name} – pause on IO",
        description=_description(tcps, active_tcp),
    )
    async def pause_on_io_program(
        ctx: nova.ProgramContext,
        wait_io: str = DEFAULT_WAIT_IO,
        wait_io_value: bool = DEFAULT_WAIT_IO_VALUE,
        stop_io: str = DEFAULT_STOP_IO,
        stop_io_value: bool = DEFAULT_STOP_IO_VALUE,
        tcp: str | None = default_tcp,
        degrees: int = DEFAULT_DEGREES,
        direction: Direction = DEFAULT_DIRECTION,
        state_rate_ms: int = DEFAULT_STATE_RATE_MS,
        stall_s: float = DEFAULT_STALL_S,
        gap_ms: int = DEFAULT_GAP_MS,
        replan: bool = DEFAULT_REPLAN,
        verbose: bool = DEFAULT_VERBOSE,
        scenario: str = DEFAULT_SCENARIO,
        enable_delay_ms: int = DEFAULT_ENABLE_DELAY_MS,
        fail_after_stall_s: float = DEFAULT_FAIL_AFTER_STALL_S,
        resume: str = DEFAULT_RESUME,
        missed_auto_resume: str = DEFAULT_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME,
    ) -> None:
        # The run's log lines also go to <LOG_DIR>/<controller>.log, so the UI's
        # Logs panel covers a program started via /programs as well (in a
        # run_program.py subprocess this is a no-op, see logs.capture_run).
        with logs.capture_run(controller_name):
            await _pause_on_io(
                ctx,
                wait_io,
                wait_io_value,
                stop_io,
                stop_io_value,
                tcp,
                degrees,
                direction,
                state_rate_ms,
                stall_s,
                gap_ms,
                replan,
                verbose,
                scenario,
                enable_delay_ms,
                fail_after_stall_s,
                resume,
                missed_auto_resume,
            )

    return pause_on_io_program


def _apply_resume_strategy(controller_name: str, resume: str, missed_auto_resume: str) -> None:
    """Set the SDK's process-wide execution policy for this run's resume strategy.

    The SDK reads the policy once per process (``NOVA_PAUSE_RESUME`` /
    ``NOVA_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME``); this app sets it from the run options instead, so
    the UI choice wins. One ``run_program.py`` process per robot keeps it per robot.
    """
    from dataclasses import replace

    from nova.cell.movement_controller.policy import (
        MissedAutoResume,
        PauseResumeStrategy,
        default_execution_policy,
        set_default_execution_policy,
    )

    policy = replace(
        default_execution_policy(),
        pause_resume=PauseResumeStrategy(resume),
        missed_auto_resume=MissedAutoResume(missed_auto_resume),
    )
    set_default_execution_policy(policy)
    logger.info(
        "%s: resume '%s' -- %s; missed auto-resume: %s (effective %s)",
        controller_name,
        resume,
        RESUME_HELP[resume],
        missed_auto_resume,
        policy.effective_missed_auto_resume.value,
    )


async def _write_enable(

import nova
from decouple import config
from nova import api
from nova.actions import joint_ptp
from nova.cell import motion_enable_signal
from nova.events import Cycle, novax_cycle
from nova.program.function import Program
from nova.types import MotionSettings
from nova.utils.io import IOChange, get_bus_io_value, set_bus_io_value, wait_for_bus_io
from novax.config import CELL_NAME
from wandelbots_api_client.v2_pydantic.models.models import SettableRobotSystemMode

from audi_arg3_pause import logs
from audi_arg3_pause.observe import ExecutionObserver

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MOTION_TIMEOUT_S = config("MOTION_TIMEOUT_S", default=0.0, cast=float)
"""Hard bound on one execute(), or 0 to disable it -- and disabled is the default here.

always a fault. In this app an execution that sits still can be completely
correct: with the enable signal low the robot is *supposed* to wait, for as long
as the operator leaves it low. A timeout would also destroy the wedged state
that the run exists to capture, so the stall detector reports instead and the
run keeps going.

``fail_after_stall_s`` is the bound that fits this app better, because it only
fires while the robot *is* allowed to move. Both are applied by
``ExecutionObserver.run_execution``, which owns the motion task.

# Trajectory locations move by more than this when the robot actually ran.
_TRAVEL_EPSILON = 1e-6

# SDK loggers that explain what the pause machinery decided. ``move_forward``
# reports every pause and resume at INFO already, so the interesting lines are
# in the log without ``verbose``; the rest are the frame-by-frame detail.
_SDK_PAUSE_LOGGERS = (
    "nova.cell.movement_controller.move_forward",
    "nova.cell.movement_controller.trajectory_cursor",
    "nova.cell.movement_controller.trajectory_state_machine",
    "nova.cell.io_condition",
)


# Run-gate IO defaults. The names match the move-up apps so the same signals
# drive every variant on a cell -- but `wait_io` means something different here
# (the enable signal for pause_on_io, see the module docstring).
DEFAULT_WAIT_IO = "start"
DEFAULT_WAIT_IO_VALUE = True
DEFAULT_STOP_IO = "stop"
DEFAULT_STOP_IO_VALUE = True

# The base-joint rotation the operator can pick, in degrees. Presets only, same
# set as ../tcpswitch.
DEGREE_PRESETS = (5, 10, 15, 20, 45, 90)
DEFAULT_DEGREES = 10
Direction = Literal["positive", "negative"]
DEFAULT_DIRECTION: Direction = "positive"

# Motion-group state stream rate in ms for the *execution*, per run. 0 = the
# controller's own step rate, requested by passing state_stream_rate_msecs=None
# -- the same meaning as in every sibling app. This is the stream the SDK's
# execution state machine reads, so it is a plausible variable in a pause bug;
# the observer's own stream has its own rate (OBSERVE_STATE_RATE_MS).
DEFAULT_STATE_RATE_MS = config("STATE_RESPONSE_RATE_MS", default=0, cast=int)

# How long "enabled, standing still, location not advancing" must hold inside
# one execute() before it is reported. 0 switches the detector off.
DEFAULT_STALL_S = config("STALL_S", default=10.0, cast=float)

# Pause between two cycles, in milliseconds. The reported symptom is about the
# execution that *follows* a finished one, so how much time sits between them
# is worth being able to vary.
DEFAULT_GAP_MS = 0

# Plan once and execute many (the move-up apps' shape) or plan every cycle.
DEFAULT_REPLAN = False

DEFAULT_VERBOSE = False

# How the enable signal is driven during a run.
#
# The default is the one that touches nothing: on a real cell this signal is a
# PLC-facing Profinet variable, and it is also what the sibling apps use as
# their run-enable -- so an app that writes it is driving every other ARG3 robot
# on the cell too. Automation is opt-in for that reason, and says so in the log.
SCENARIO_MANUAL = "manual"
SCENARIO_ENABLED_ONCE = "enabled_once"
SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME = "auto_resume"
SCENARIOS = (SCENARIO_MANUAL, SCENARIO_ENABLED_ONCE, SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME)
DEFAULT_SCENARIO = SCENARIO_MANUAL

SCENARIO_HELP = {
    SCENARIO_MANUAL: (
        "the app never writes the enable signal; the operator toggles it. Use this to watch "
        "a long run, or to reproduce by hand."
    ),
    SCENARIO_ENABLED_ONCE: (
        "reads the enable signal but never writes it. Waits until it already allows motion, "
        "then commands exactly ONE "
        "execution and finish. No pause and no resume are involved, so a robot that does not "
        "move here has failed to start from a clean state -- run it repeatedly, each run in a "
        "fresh process, and count."
    ),
    SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME: (
        "per cycle: drop the enable signal, command the execution (the robot is held at the "
        "start), wait `enable_delay_ms`, raise the signal again and let the cycle run. This "
        "exercises the pause/resume path unattended, which is where the wedge was observed."
    ),
}

# Who resumes an IO pause (the SDK's ExecutionPolicy.pause_resume, ADR 002 addendum).
# Not to be confused with the auto_resume *scenario* above, which is about the app
# driving the enable signal; this is about who restarts the motion afterwards.
RESUME_SDK = "sdk"
RESUME_CONTROLLER = "controller"
RESUME_STRATEGIES = (RESUME_SDK, RESUME_CONTROLLER)
DEFAULT_RESUME = RESUME_SDK
RESUME_HELP = {
    RESUME_SDK: (
        "the SDK sends a new start once the enable signal allows motion again (the controller "
        "never resumes a plain pause_on_io pause by itself)"
    ),
    RESUME_CONTROLLER: (
        "every start carries PauseOnIO.auto_resume and the controller resumes by itself "
        "(robotics/wbr!2384; needs a RAE image and API client built with it)"
    ),
}
# Under 'controller': what the SDK does when the signal allows motion but the
# controller still holds the robot after the SDK's resume_detect_s.
MISSED_FAIL = "fail"
MISSED_START = "start"
MISSED_AUTO_RESUME_CHOICES = (MISSED_FAIL, MISSED_START)
DEFAULT_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME = MISSED_FAIL

# Pause between dropping the enable signal and commanding the execution, so the
# controller has seen the new value before it is armed with the condition.
ENABLE_SETTLE_MS = config("ENABLE_SETTLE_MS", default=300, cast=int)

# Delay between an execution being commanded and the enable signal being raised
# again, in the auto_resume scenario.
DEFAULT_ENABLE_DELAY_MS = 1000

# End a cycle that has been "allowed to move but standing still" for this long.
# 0 = never, which keeps a wedge parked for inspection; set it for unattended runs.
DEFAULT_FAIL_AFTER_STALL_S = config("FAIL_AFTER_STALL_S", default=0.0, cast=float)

# Motion limits. Same reasoning as ../tcpswitch: TCP limits bound a joint PTP
# too, so a KR240's flange at ~1.5 m radius rotates at most ~8 deg/s at 200 mm/s.
TCP_VELOCITY_MM_S = config("TCP_VELOCITY_MM_S", default=200.0, cast=float)
TCP_ACCELERATION_MM_S2 = config("TCP_ACCELERATION_MM_S2", default=500.0, cast=float)
TCP_JERK_MM_S3 = config("TCP_JERK_MM_S3", default=2500.0, cast=float)

# Tag on the cycle events this app publishes (nova.v2.cells.<cell>.cycle), so a
# consumer can tell them from the other apps' cycles on the same cell.
APP_NAME = "audi-arg3-pause"
PROGRAM_SUFFIX = "_pause_on_io"


def program_id(controller_name: str) -> str:
    """The NOVAx program id for a controller -- the one place it is derived."""
    return f"{controller_name}{PROGRAM_SUFFIX}"


def validate_run_settings(
    degrees: int,
    direction: str,
    stall_s: float,
    gap_ms: int,
    scenario: str = DEFAULT_SCENARIO,
    enable_delay_ms: int = DEFAULT_ENABLE_DELAY_MS,
    resume: str = DEFAULT_RESUME,
    missed_auto_resume: str = DEFAULT_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME,
) -> None:
    """Reject bad run settings up front, with a message the operator can act on."""
    if scenario not in SCENARIOS:
        raise ValueError(f"scenario must be one of {SCENARIOS}, got '{scenario}'")
    if resume not in RESUME_STRATEGIES:
        raise ValueError(f"resume must be one of {RESUME_STRATEGIES}, got '{resume}'")
    if missed_auto_resume not in MISSED_AUTO_RESUME_CHOICES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"missed_auto_resume must be one of {MISSED_AUTO_RESUME_CHOICES}, "
            f"got '{missed_auto_resume}'"
        )
    if enable_delay_ms < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"enable_delay_ms must not be negative, got {enable_delay_ms}")
    if degrees not in DEGREE_PRESETS:
        raise ValueError(f"degrees must be one of {DEGREE_PRESETS}, got {degrees}")
    if direction not in ("positive", "negative"):
        raise ValueError(f"direction must be 'positive' or 'negative', got '{direction}'")
    if stall_s < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"stall_s must not be negative, got {stall_s}")
    if gap_ms < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"gap_ms must not be negative, got {gap_ms}")


def wire_rate(state_rate_ms: int) -> int | None:
    """``state_rate_ms`` as the SDK wants it: 0 means "don't ask for a rate"."""
    return state_rate_ms or None


def enable_condition(io: str, enable_value: bool) -> api.models.PauseOnIO:
    """The ``pause_on_io`` condition for an enable signal on bus IO ``io``.

    ``motion_enable_signal`` is the SDK's fail-safe wiring: it pauses while
    ``io == False``, so a dropped signal, a broken wire or a lost fieldbus all
    stop the robot. ``enable_value=False`` inverts that, which is what the
    operator gets by unticking the value in the UI -- it is supported so the
    field means what it says, but it is *not* fail-safe and says so in the log.
    """
    if enable_value:
        return motion_enable_signal(io, api.models.IOOrigin.BUS_IO)
    logger.warning(
        "enable IO '%s' is configured to allow motion while it reads False; this inverted "
        "wiring is NOT fail-safe (a lost bus reads False and would allow motion)",
        io,
    )
    return api.models.PauseOnIO(
        io=api.models.IOBooleanValue(io=io, value=True),
        comparator=api.models.Comparator.COMPARATOR_EQUALS,
        io_origin=api.models.IOOrigin.BUS_IO,
    )


def _set_sdk_verbosity(verbose: bool) -> None:
    """Turn the SDK's pause/cursor/state-machine loggers up for this run."""
    for name in _SDK_PAUSE_LOGGERS:
        logging.getLogger(name).setLevel(logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.NOTSET)


def _sdk_version() -> str:
    """The installed wandelbots-nova version, for the top of every run's log.

    Which SDK branch produced a log is the first question asked of it, and the
    answer must not depend on remembering what was pinned that day.
    """
    try:
        return version("wandelbots-nova")
    except PackageNotFoundError:  # pragma: no cover - only if the SDK is not installed
        return "unknown"


def _new_cycle_event(ctx: nova.ProgramContext, controller_name: str, cycle: int) -> Cycle:
    """A cycle event for one motion, published on ``nova.v2.cells.<cell>.cycle``."""
    return novax_cycle(
        ctx.cell,
        app=APP_NAME,
        program=program_id(controller_name),
        extra={"controller": controller_name, "cycle": cycle},
    )


async def _publish_cycle(publish, controller_name: str, what: str) -> None:
    """Await one of ``Cycle.start()/finish()/fail()`` without letting it hurt the run.

    A broken event bus must never stop or fail a motion. Deliberately NOT
    ``async with Cycle``: its ``__aexit__`` would swallow the motion's own
    exception, turning a failed robot into one that quietly keeps cycling.
    """
    try:
        await publish
    except Exception:
        logger.debug("%s: could not publish cycle %s event", controller_name, what, exc_info=True)


async def create_pause_program(controller_name: str, nova_instance: nova.Nova) -> Program:
    """Create the pause-on-IO program for one controller.

    The returned ``Program`` can be registered on a ``Novax`` instance; its id
    is derived from the controller name (see ``program_id``).
    """
    tcps, active_tcp = await tcp_choices(controller_name, nova_instance)
    default_tcp = active_tcp or (tcps[0] if tcps else None)

    async def _pause_on_io(
        ctx: nova.ProgramContext,
        wait_io: str,
        wait_io_value: bool,
        stop_io: str,
        stop_io_value: bool,
        tcp: str | None,
        degrees: int,
        direction: str,
        state_rate_ms: int,
        stall_s: float,
        gap_ms: int,
        replan: bool,
        verbose: bool,
        scenario: str,
        enable_delay_ms: int,
        fail_after_stall_s: float,
        resume: str,
        missed_auto_resume: str,
    ) -> None:
        validate_run_settings(
            degrees,
            direction,
            stall_s,
            gap_ms,
            scenario,
            enable_delay_ms,
            resume,
            missed_auto_resume,
        )
        _set_sdk_verbosity(verbose)
        _apply_resume_strategy(controller_name, resume, missed_auto_resume)
        sign = 1.0 if direction == "positive" else -1.0
        delta_rad = sign * math.radians(degrees)

        motion_group = controller[0]

            "'%s' ends the loop at %s",
            controller_name,
            wait_io,
            wait_io_value,
            stop_io,
            stop_io_value,
        )
        logger.info(
            "%s: tcp=%s, joint 0 %s%d deg and back, state_rate=%s, stall_s=%.1f, gap_ms=%d, "
            "replan=%s, verbose=%s, motion_timeout=%s, fail_after_stall=%s",
            controller_name,
            tcp,
            "+" if sign > 0 else "-",
            degrees,
            f"{state_rate_ms} ms" if state_rate_ms else "controller step rate",
            stall_s,
            gap_ms,
            replan,
            verbose,
            f"{MOTION_TIMEOUT_S:.0f}s" if MOTION_TIMEOUT_S > 0 else "disabled",
            f"{fail_after_stall_s:.0f}s" if fail_after_stall_s > 0 else "disabled",

        "move here has failed to start from a clean state -- run it repeatedly, each run in a "
        "fresh process, and count."
    ),
    SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME: (
        "per cycle: drop the enable signal, command the execution (the robot is held at the "
        "start), wait `enable_delay_ms`, raise the signal again and let the cycle run. This "
        "exercises the pause/resume path unattended, which is where the wedge was observed."
    ),
}

# Who resumes an IO pause (the SDK's ExecutionPolicy.pause_resume, ADR 002 addendum).
# Not to be confused with the auto_resume *scenario* above, which is about the app
# driving the enable signal; this is about who restarts the motion afterwards.
RESUME_SDK = "sdk"
RESUME_CONTROLLER = "controller"
RESUME_STRATEGIES = (RESUME_SDK, RESUME_CONTROLLER)
DEFAULT_RESUME = RESUME_SDK
RESUME_HELP = {
    RESUME_SDK: (
        "the SDK sends a new start once the enable signal allows motion again (the controller "
        "never resumes a plain pause_on_io pause by itself)"
    ),
    RESUME_CONTROLLER: (
        "every start carries PauseOnIO.auto_resume and the controller resumes by itself "
        "(robotics/wbr!2384; needs a RAE image and API client built with it)"
    ),
}
# Under 'controller': what the SDK does when the signal allows motion but the
# controller still holds the robot after the SDK's resume_detect_s.
MISSED_FAIL = "fail"
MISSED_START = "start"
MISSED_AUTO_RESUME_CHOICES = (MISSED_FAIL, MISSED_START)
DEFAULT_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME = MISSED_FAIL

# Pause between dropping the enable signal and commanding the execution, so the
# controller has seen the new value before it is armed with the condition.
ENABLE_SETTLE_MS = config("ENABLE_SETTLE_MS", default=300, cast=int)

# Delay between an execution being commanded and the enable signal being raised
# again, in the auto_resume scenario.
DEFAULT_ENABLE_DELAY_MS = 1000

# End a cycle that has been "allowed to move but standing still" for this long.
# 0 = never, which keeps a wedge parked for inspection; set it for unattended runs.
DEFAULT_FAIL_AFTER_STALL_S = config("FAIL_AFTER_STALL_S", default=0.0, cast=float)

# Motion limits. Same reasoning as ../tcpswitch: TCP limits bound a joint PTP
# too, so a KR240's flange at ~1.5 m radius rotates at most ~8 deg/s at 200 mm/s.
TCP_VELOCITY_MM_S = config("TCP_VELOCITY_MM_S", default=200.0, cast=float)
TCP_ACCELERATION_MM_S2 = config("TCP_ACCELERATION_MM_S2", default=500.0, cast=float)
TCP_JERK_MM_S3 = config("TCP_JERK_MM_S3", default=2500.0, cast=float)

# Tag on the cycle events this app publishes (nova.v2.cells.<cell>.cycle), so a
# consumer can tell them from the other apps' cycles on the same cell.
APP_NAME = "audi-arg3-pause"
PROGRAM_SUFFIX = "_pause_on_io"


def program_id(controller_name: str) -> str:
    """The NOVAx program id for a controller -- the one place it is derived."""
    return f"{controller_name}{PROGRAM_SUFFIX}"


def validate_run_settings(
    degrees: int,
    direction: str,
    stall_s: float,
    gap_ms: int,
    scenario: str = DEFAULT_SCENARIO,
    enable_delay_ms: int = DEFAULT_ENABLE_DELAY_MS,
    resume: str = DEFAULT_RESUME,
    missed_auto_resume: str = DEFAULT_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME,
) -> None:
    """Reject bad run settings up front, with a message the operator can act on."""
    if scenario not in SCENARIOS:
        raise ValueError(f"scenario must be one of {SCENARIOS}, got '{scenario}'")
    if resume not in RESUME_STRATEGIES:
        raise ValueError(f"resume must be one of {RESUME_STRATEGIES}, got '{resume}'")
    if missed_auto_resume not in MISSED_AUTO_RESUME_CHOICES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"missed_auto_resume must be one of {MISSED_AUTO_RESUME_CHOICES}, "
            f"got '{missed_auto_resume}'"
        )
    if enable_delay_ms < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"enable_delay_ms must not be negative, got {enable_delay_ms}")
    if degrees not in DEGREE_PRESETS:
        raise ValueError(f"degrees must be one of {DEGREE_PRESETS}, got {degrees}")
    if direction not in ("positive", "negative"):
        raise ValueError(f"direction must be 'positive' or 'negative', got '{direction}'")
    if stall_s < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"stall_s must not be negative, got {stall_s}")
    if gap_ms < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"gap_ms must not be negative, got {gap_ms}")


def wire_rate(state_rate_ms: int) -> int | None:
    """``state_rate_ms`` as the SDK wants it: 0 means "don't ask for a rate"."""
    return state_rate_ms or None


def enable_condition(io: str, enable_value: bool) -> api.models.PauseOnIO:
    """The ``pause_on_io`` condition for an enable signal on bus IO ``io``.

    ``motion_enable_signal`` is the SDK's fail-safe wiring: it pauses while
    ``io == False``, so a dropped signal, a broken wire or a lost fieldbus all
    stop the robot. ``enable_value=False`` inverts that, which is what the
    operator gets by unticking the value in the UI -- it is supported so the
    field means what it says, but it is *not* fail-safe and says so in the log.
    """
    if enable_value:
        return motion_enable_signal(io, api.models.IOOrigin.BUS_IO)
    logger.warning(
        "enable IO '%s' is configured to allow motion while it reads False; this inverted "
        "wiring is NOT fail-safe (a lost bus reads False and would allow motion)",
        io,
    )
    return api.models.PauseOnIO(
        io=api.models.IOBooleanValue(io=io, value=True),
        comparator=api.models.Comparator.COMPARATOR_EQUALS,
        io_origin=api.models.IOOrigin.BUS_IO,
    )


def _set_sdk_verbosity(verbose: bool) -> None:
    """Turn the SDK's pause/cursor/state-machine loggers up for this run."""
    for name in _SDK_PAUSE_LOGGERS:
        logging.getLogger(name).setLevel(logging.DEBUG if verbose else logging.NOTSET)


def _sdk_version() -> str:
    """The installed wandelbots-nova version, for the top of every run's log.

    Which SDK branch produced a log is the first question asked of it, and the
    answer must not depend on remembering what was pinned that day.
    """
    try:
        return version("wandelbots-nova")
    except PackageNotFoundError:  # pragma: no cover - only if the SDK is not installed
        return "unknown"


def _new_cycle_event(ctx: nova.ProgramContext, controller_name: str, cycle: int) -> Cycle:
    """A cycle event for one motion, published on ``nova.v2.cells.<cell>.cycle``."""
    return novax_cycle(
        ctx.cell,
        app=APP_NAME,
        program=program_id(controller_name),
        extra={"controller": controller_name, "cycle": cycle},
    )


async def _publish_cycle(publish, controller_name: str, what: str) -> None:
    """Await one of ``Cycle.start()/finish()/fail()`` without letting it hurt the run.

    A broken event bus must never stop or fail a motion. Deliberately NOT
    ``async with Cycle``: its ``__aexit__`` would swallow the motion's own
    exception, turning a failed robot into one that quietly keeps cycling.
    """
    try:
        await publish
    except Exception:
        logger.debug("%s: could not publish cycle %s event", controller_name, what, exc_info=True)


async def create_pause_program(controller_name: str, nova_instance: nova.Nova) -> Program:
    """Create the pause-on-IO program for one controller.

    The returned ``Program`` can be registered on a ``Novax`` instance; its id
    is derived from the controller name (see ``program_id``).
    """
    tcps, active_tcp = await tcp_choices(controller_name, nova_instance)
    default_tcp = active_tcp or (tcps[0] if tcps else None)

    async def _pause_on_io(
        ctx: nova.ProgramContext,
        wait_io: str,
        wait_io_value: bool,
        stop_io: str,
        stop_io_value: bool,
        tcp: str | None,
        degrees: int,
        direction: str,
        state_rate_ms: int,
        stall_s: float,
        gap_ms: int,
        replan: bool,
        verbose: bool,
        scenario: str,
        enable_delay_ms: int,
        fail_after_stall_s: float,
        resume: str,
        missed_auto_resume: str,
    ) -> None:
        validate_run_settings(
            degrees,
            direction,
            stall_s,
            gap_ms,
            scenario,
            enable_delay_ms,
            resume,
            missed_auto_resume,
        )
        _set_sdk_verbosity(verbose)
        _apply_resume_strategy(controller_name, resume, missed_auto_resume)
        sign = 1.0 if direction == "positive" else -1.0
        delta_rad = sign * math.radians(degrees)

        controller = await ctx.cell.controller(controller_name)
        motion_group = controller[0]
        pause_on_io = enable_condition(wait_io, wait_io_value)

        logger.info(
            "%s: pause-on-IO repro -- enable IO '%s' allows motion while it reads %s, stop IO "
            "'%s' ends the loop at %s",
            controller_name,
            wait_io,
            wait_io_value,
            stop_io,
            stop_io_value,
        )
        logger.info(
            "%s: tcp=%s, joint 0 %s%d deg and back, state_rate=%s, stall_s=%.1f, gap_ms=%d, "
            "replan=%s, verbose=%s, motion_timeout=%s, fail_after_stall=%s",
            controller_name,
            tcp,
            "+" if sign > 0 else "-",
            degrees,
            f"{state_rate_ms} ms" if state_rate_ms else "controller step rate",
            stall_s,
            gap_ms,
            replan,
            verbose,
            f"{MOTION_TIMEOUT_S:.0f}s" if MOTION_TIMEOUT_S > 0 else "disabled",
            f"{fail_after_stall_s:.0f}s" if fail_after_stall_s > 0 else "disabled",
        )
        logger.info("%s: scenario '%s' -- %s", controller_name, scenario, SCENARIO_HELP[scenario])
        if scenario == SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME:
            # The only scenario that drives the signal. It is a PLC-facing
            # variable that the sibling apps use as their run-enable, so an app
            # writing it is driving every other ARG3 robot on the cell too.
            logger.warning(
                "%s: this run WRITES the enable IO '%s' itself, once per cycle. On a shared "
                "cell that signal also gates the sibling apps' robots.",
                controller_name,
                wait_io,
            )
        if scenario == SCENARIO_AUTO_RESUME and fail_after_stall_s <= 0:
            logger.warning(
                "%s: scenario '%s' is meant to run unattended but fail_after_stall_s is 0, so a "
                "wedged cycle will park the robot until someone stops it",
                controller_name,
                scenario,
            )
        logger.info(
            "%s: wandelbots-nova %s; pause condition sent to the controller: %s",
            controller_name,
            _sdk_version(),
            pause_on_io.model_dump_json(),
        )

        # Switch controller default usage to control mode before moving.
        await ctx.nova.api.controller_api.set_default_mode(
            cell=CELL_NAME,
            controller=controller_name,
            mode=SettableRobotSystemMode.MODE_CONTROL,
        )

        settings = MotionSettings(
            tcp_velocity_limit=TCP_VELOCITY_MM_S,
            REDACTED,
            tcp_jerk_limit=TCP_JERK_MM_S3,
        )

        # Home is read once: every cycle rotates away from and back to the same
        # joint configuration, so the robot never drifts across cycles.
        home = tuple(await motion_group.joints())

                await _publish_cycle(cycle_event.start(), controller_name, "started")
                started = time.monotonic()
                releaser = None

def _apply_resume_strategy(controller_name: str, resume: str, missed_auto_resume: str) -> None:
    """Set the SDK's process-wide execution policy for this run's resume strategy.

    The SDK reads the policy once per process (``NOVA_PAUSE_RESUME`` /
    ``NOVA_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME``); this app sets it from the run options instead, so
    the UI choice wins. One ``run_program.py`` process per robot keeps it per robot.
    """
    from dataclasses import replace

    from nova.cell.movement_controller.policy import (
        MissedAutoResume,
        PauseResumeStrategy,
        default_execution_policy,
        set_default_execution_policy,
    )

    policy = replace(
        default_execution_policy(),
        pause_resume=PauseResumeStrategy(resume),
        missed_auto_resume=MissedAutoResume(missed_auto_resume),
    )
    set_default_execution_policy(policy)
    logger.info(
        "%s: resume '%s' -- %s; missed auto-resume: %s (effective %s)",
        controller_name,
        resume,
        RESUME_HELP[resume],
        missed_auto_resume,
        policy.effective_missed_auto_resume.value,
    )


async def _write_enable(
    nova_instance, io: str, value: bool, controller_name: str, cycle: int, what: str
) -> None:
    """Write the enable signal, and make the write itself part of the evidence.

    Every automated write is logged before the fact: when a resume later fails,
    the first question is whether the signal was actually driven, and an entry
    written by the app is the answer that does not depend on the watcher.
    """
    logger.info(
        "%s: cycle %d -- %s: setting enable IO '%s' = %s", controller_name, cycle, what, io, value
    )
    await set_bus_io_value({io: value}, nova=nova_instance, cell=CELL_NAME)


async def _release_after(
    nova_instance, io: str, value: bool, delay_ms: int, controller_name: str, cycle: int
) -> None:
    """Raise the enable signal ``delay_ms`` after the execution was commanded.

    Runs beside the execution rather than before it: the robot has to be held at
    the start of its trajectory first, so the release is what the pause/resume
    path is being tested with. Cancelled if the execution ends first.
    """
    await asyncio.sleep(delay_ms / 1000.0)
    await _write_enable(nova_instance, io, value, controller_name, cycle, "releasing")


async def _wait_for_enable(
    nova_instance, io: str, value: bool, controller_name: str, cycle: int
) -> None:
    """Block until the enable signal already allows motion.

    The only place in this app where a signal is waited on *before* an
    execution, and it is the definition of the pre-enabled scenario rather than
    a gate: the question it asks is whether an execution commanded with nothing
    to pause it starts at all.
    """
    current = await get_bus_io_value([io], nova=nova_instance, cell=CELL_NAME)
    if current.get(io) == value:
        logger.info(
            "%s: cycle %d -- enable IO '%s' is already %s, commanding the execution",
            controller_name,
            cycle,
            io,
            value,
        )
        return
    logger.info(
        "%s: cycle %d -- waiting for enable IO '%s' to become %s before commanding anything",
        controller_name,
        cycle,
        io,
        value,
    )
    await wait_for_bus_io(
        [io],
        on_change=lambda changes: _io_reached(changes, io, value),
        nova=nova_instance,
        cell=CELL_NAME,
    )
    logger.info("%s: cycle %d -- enable IO '%s' is %s", controller_name, cycle, io, value)


def _io_reached(changes: dict[str, IOChange], io: str, expected: bool) -> bool:
    """Return True once ``io`` reads ``expected`` (the wait_for_bus_io callback)."""
    change = changes.get(io)
    return change is not None and change.new_value == expected


def _report_verdict(controller_name: str, cycle: int, travelled: float) -> None:
    """State plainly whether the robot moved in this execution.

    ``execute()`` returning says nothing about whether the robot went anywhere
    -- that is the whole point of this app -- so the verdict is its own line,
    greppable, on every cycle.
    """
    if travelled > _TRAVEL_EPSILON:
        return
    logger.error(
        "%s: cycle %d -- REPRODUCED: execute() returned but the robot never moved (travelled %.4f)",
        controller_name,
        cycle,
        travelled,
    )


async def _plan(motion_group, actions, tcp: str | None, controller_name: str, cycle: int):
    """Plan the trajectory and log how long it took."""
    started = time.monotonic()
    trajectory = await motion_group.plan(actions, tcp)
    logger.info(
        "%s: %s -- planned with tcp '%s' in %.3fs (%d samples)",
        controller_name,
        f"cycle {cycle}" if cycle else "once, before the first cycle",
        tcp,
        time.monotonic() - started,
        len(trajectory.joint_positions),
    )
    return trajectory


def _description(tcps: list[str], active_tcp: str | None) -> str:
    """Human-readable note for the NOVAx program description."""
    base = (
        "Rotates joint 0 by N degrees and back, every cycle, with pause_on_io armed on the "
        "enable signal -- the robot moves only while that signal reads True."
    )
    if not tcps:
        return f"{base} No TCP data."
    return f"{base} Available TCPs: {', '.join(tcps)}" + (
        f" (active '{active_tcp}')." if active_tcp else "."
    )


def _fmt(joints: tuple[float, ...]) -> str:
    return "[" + ", ".join(f"{value:.4f}" for value in joints) + "]"

    """Set the SDK's process-wide execution policy for this run's resume strategy.

    The SDK reads the policy once per process (``NOVA_PAUSE_RESUME`` /
    ``NOVA_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME``); this app sets it from the run options instead, so
    the UI choice wins. One ``run_program.py`` process per robot keeps it per robot.
    """
    from dataclasses import replace

    from nova.cell.movement_controller.policy import (
        MissedAutoResume,
        PauseResumeStrategy,
        default_execution_policy,
        set_default_execution_policy,
    )

    policy = replace(
        default_execution_policy(),
        pause_resume=PauseResumeStrategy(resume),
        missed_auto_resume=MissedAutoResume(missed_auto_resume),
    )
    set_default_execution_policy(policy)
    logger.info(
        "%s: resume '%s' -- %s; missed auto-resume: %s (effective %s)",
        controller_name,

    nova_instance, io: str, value: bool, controller_name: str, cycle: int, what: str
) -> None:
    """Write the enable signal, and make the write itself part of the evidence.

    Every automated write is logged before the fact: when a resume later fails,
    the first question is whether the signal was actually driven, and an entry
    written by the app is the answer that does not depend on the watcher.
    """
    logger.info(
        "%s: cycle %d -- %s: setting enable IO '%s' = %s", controller_name, cycle, what, io, value
    )
    await set_bus_io_value({io: value}, nova=nova_instance, cell=CELL_NAME)


async def _release_after(
    nova_instance, io: str, value: bool, delay_ms: int, controller_name: str, cycle: int
) -> None:
    """Raise the enable signal ``delay_ms`` after the execution was commanded.

    Runs beside the execution rather than before it: the robot has to be held at
    the start of its trajectory first, so the release is what the pause/resume
    path is being tested with. Cancelled if the execution ends first.
    """
    await asyncio.sleep(delay_ms / 1000.0)
    await _write_enable(nova_instance, io, value, controller_name, cycle, "releasing")


async def _wait_for_enable(
    nova_instance, io: str, value: bool, controller_name: str, cycle: int
) -> None:
    """Block until the enable signal already allows motion.

    The only place in this app where a signal is waited on *before* an
    execution, and it is the definition of the pre-enabled scenario rather than
    a gate: the question it asks is whether an execution commanded with nothing
    to pause it starts at all.
    """
    current = await get_bus_io_value([io], nova=nova_instance, cell=CELL_NAME)
    if current.get(io) == value:
        logger.info(
            "%s: cycle %d -- enable IO '%s' is already %s, commanding the execution",
            controller_name,
            cycle,
            io,
            value,
        )
        return
    logger.info(
        "%s: cycle %d -- waiting for enable IO '%s' to become %s before commanding anything",
        controller_name,
        cycle,
        io,
        value,
    )
    await wait_for_bus_io(
        [io],
        on_change=lambda changes: _io_reached(changes, io, value),
        nova=nova_instance,
        cell=CELL_NAME,
    )
    logger.info("%s: cycle %d -- enable IO '%s' is %s", controller_name, cycle, io, value)

    """Return True once ``io`` reads ``expected`` (the wait_for_bus_io callback)."""
    change = changes.get(io)
    return change is not None and change.new_value == expected

"""Standalone runner for one controller's pause-on-IO program.

Usage::

    python -m audi_arg3_pause.run_program <controller> [--tcp 1]
        [--degrees 10] [--direction positive|negative]
        [--wait-io NAME] [--wait-io-value BOOL] [--stop-io NAME] [--stop-io-value BOOL]
        [--state-rate-ms 0] [--stall-s 10] [--gap-ms 0] [--replan BOOL] [--verbose BOOL]
        [--scenario manual|enabled_once|auto_resume] [--enable-delay-ms 1000]
        [--fail-after-stall-s 0] [--resume sdk|controller] [--missed-auto-resume fail|start]

``--wait-io`` is the **enable signal**: the robot is allowed to move while it
reads ``--wait-io-value``, enforced by the controller through ``pause_on_io``.
It is not a pre-motion gate (see ``programs.py``).

Runs the program and blocks until it finishes. This is the subprocess
``runner.py`` spawns per robot; it writes its own log file and never talks to
the parent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import logging

from nova import Nova, run_program

from audi_arg3_pause.logs import configure_worker_logging
from audi_arg3_pause.programs import (
    DEFAULT_DEGREES,
    DEFAULT_DIRECTION,
    DEFAULT_ENABLE_DELAY_MS,
    DEFAULT_FAIL_AFTER_STALL_S,
    DEFAULT_GAP_MS,
    DEFAULT_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME,
    DEFAULT_REPLAN,
    DEFAULT_RESUME,
    DEFAULT_SCENARIO,
    DEFAULT_STALL_S,
    DEFAULT_STATE_RATE_MS,
    DEFAULT_STOP_IO,
    DEFAULT_STOP_IO_VALUE,
    DEFAULT_VERBOSE,
    DEFAULT_WAIT_IO,
    DEFAULT_WAIT_IO_VALUE,
    MISSED_AUTO_RESUME_CHOICES,
    RESUME_STRATEGIES,
    SCENARIOS,
    create_pause_program,
    validate_run_settings,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _parse_bool(value: str) -> bool:
    return value.lower() in ("1", "true", "yes")


async def _create_program(controller_name: str):
    """Instantiate a Nova client to inspect the controller and build the program."""
    async with Nova() as n:
        return await create_pause_program(controller_name, n)


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run one controller's pause-on-IO program")
    parser.add_argument("controller", help="Controller name")
    parser.add_argument("--tcp", default=None, help="TCP id (default: the controller's active one)")
    parser.add_argument("--degrees", type=int, default=DEFAULT_DEGREES)
    parser.add_argument("--direction", default=DEFAULT_DIRECTION)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--wait-io", default=DEFAULT_WAIT_IO, help="enable signal armed as pause_on_io"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--wait-io-value", type=_parse_bool, default=DEFAULT_WAIT_IO_VALUE)
    parser.add_argument("--stop-io", default=DEFAULT_STOP_IO)
    parser.add_argument("--stop-io-value", type=_parse_bool, default=DEFAULT_STOP_IO_VALUE)
    parser.add_argument("--state-rate-ms", type=int, default=DEFAULT_STATE_RATE_MS)
    parser.add_argument("--stall-s", type=float, default=DEFAULT_STALL_S)
    parser.add_argument("--gap-ms", type=int, default=DEFAULT_GAP_MS)
    parser.add_argument("--replan", type=_parse_bool, default=DEFAULT_REPLAN)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--scenario",
        default=DEFAULT_SCENARIO,
        choices=SCENARIOS,
        help="how the enable signal is driven; only 'manual' never writes it",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--enable-delay-ms", type=int, default=DEFAULT_ENABLE_DELAY_MS)
    parser.add_argument("--fail-after-stall-s", type=float, default=DEFAULT_FAIL_AFTER_STALL_S)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--resume",
        default=DEFAULT_RESUME,
        choices=RESUME_STRATEGIES,
        help="who resumes an IO pause: the SDK (new start) or the controller (auto_resume)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--missed-auto-resume",
        default=DEFAULT_MISSED_AUTO_RESUME,
        choices=MISSED_AUTO_RESUME_CHOICES,
        help="under --resume controller: fail, or send one start, when it does not resume",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", type=_parse_bool, default=DEFAULT_VERBOSE)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    # Own rotating log file, not the parent's stdout -- the parent never reads
    # this process's output (see runner.py).
    configure_worker_logging(args.controller)

    try:
        validate_run_settings(
            args.degrees,
            args.direction,
            args.stall_s,
            args.gap_ms,
            args.scenario,
            args.enable_delay_ms,
            args.resume,
            args.missed_auto_resume,
        )
        program = asyncio.run(_create_program(args.controller))
        inputs = {
            "wait_io": args.wait_io,
            "wait_io_value": args.wait_io_value,
            "stop_io": args.stop_io,
            "stop_io_value": args.stop_io_value,
            "tcp": args.tcp,
            "degrees": args.degrees,
            "direction": args.direction,
            "state_rate_ms": args.state_rate_ms,
            "stall_s": args.stall_s,
            "gap_ms": args.gap_ms,
            "replan": args.replan,
            "verbose": args.verbose,
            "scenario": args.scenario,
            "enable_delay_ms": args.enable_delay_ms,
            "fail_after_stall_s": args.fail_after_stall_s,
            "resume": args.resume,
            "missed_auto_resume": args.missed_auto_resume,
        }
        run_program(program, inputs=inputs, sync=True)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        logger.info("%s: interrupted, shutting down", args.controller)
    except Exception:
        # The parent does not read our output, so an unlogged traceback would be
        # lost entirely -- and a failure is exactly what this app is hunting for.
        logger.exception("%s: run failed", args.controller)
        raise


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
